idiom_name: rust-rdkafka Message::headers() plus HashMap<SequenceId, Vec<Option<Bytes>>> reassembly
implementation_notes: rust-rdkafka exposes message headers through Message::headers() and MessageHeaders::iter(), and librdkafka preserves per-partition order, so the three fields ride in the header map and the receiver owns a HashMap of partially filled groups; StreamConsumer yields messages in per-partition order for a while-let loop. Nothing in the crate implements completeness or release, so the classic structure - parse header, index by position, release on end marker, reap on timeout - is the realization, with tokio::sync::mpsc covering the in-process ordered case.
pitfalls: MessageHeaders::get returns the first matching header and headers are optional: treat a missing sequence header as a protocol error instead of defaulting silently.
Bytes borrows from the message, so a part stored across loop iterations must be copied into an owned buffer or the borrow checker rejects it.
A HashMap of groups grows without bound unless a sweeper task reaps incomplete sequences.
